title.value: GitHub Repositories with Links to Academic Papers: Public Access, Traceability, and Evolution
title.justification: The title accurately captures the main topics explored in the paper, focusing on the connections between GitHub repositories and academic papers regarding public access, traceability, and evolution of these links.
title.quote: GitHub Repositories with Links to Academic Papers: Public Access, Traceability, and Evolution

extractions.description: The paper investigates the links between GitHub repositories and academic papers, with a focus on public access, traceability, and the evolution of these connections. It conducts a large-scale study of over 20,000 GitHub repositories to explore how these links are established and maintained, typically found in the README files of the repositories. The study aims to understand issues of public access and how traceable these academic references are within connected repositories.

primary_category.justification: The paper focuses on traceability and public access of academic papers in GitHub repositories, which does not directly align with the specified eco-responsible categories related to environmental, sustainable, or climate-related objectives.
primary_category.quote: This paper investigates the role of academic paper references contained in these repositories.

secondary_categories.justification: The study does not directly relate to any eco-responsible areas like climate change, natural systems protection, or similar categories as listed.
secondary_categories.quote: The main goal of our study is to gain insights into the links between software repositories on GitHub and academic papers.

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper does not fit into any of the eco-responsible sub-categories provided, as its focal points are more about scientific collaboration and traceability via GitHub rather than specific environmental impacts.
primary_sub_category.quote: Although referencing a paper is not typical, we find that a vast majority of referenced academic papers are public access.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: There are no relevant sub-categories as the topic of GitHub repository linkage to academic papers does not correlate with eco-responsible applications or technologies.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Keeping up with the state of the art (SOTA) between software repositories and papers is always a challenge, especially due to the differences in cultures between scientists and software engineers.

new_primary_category.justification: The primary focus of the paper is on improving scientific collaboration through the traceability of academic papers linked to software repositories, which suggests a new category beyond the provided eco-responsible options.
new_primary_category.quote: This paper investigates the role of academic paper references contained in these repositories.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The sub-category aligns with the paper's discussion on how open-source software on platforms like GitHub enhances the accessibility and traceability of academic work.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: software that is developed during the scientific research process is often released as open source software (OSS) to promote reproducible research.
